guideTitle: Best Cordless String Trimmers with Batteries Included (2026)
metaTitle: Best Cordless String Trimmers with Batteries
metaDescription: Six cordless string trimmer kits with batteries and chargers in the box, compared on pack size, charger speed and what you really get for runtime per mow.
expertTake: The Craftsman V20 kit with a 4Ah battery is the best complete package from an established platform, and the two 4.0Ah kit is the best for runtime on a budget. The Greenworks 24V is the pick for beginners who want a telescoping shaft. Skip any kit that does not state its battery size, because that number decides how long you can cut.
introParagraphs: A trimmer that ships with its battery and charger lets you cut on day one, but the contents of the box decide how long the job takes. A small pack that runs flat after a short session turns a convenient kit into a stop-start chore.

The figures to read are the pack capacity, the number of packs and the charger, not just the headline speed. This guide compares six complete kits on what you actually get in the box and what that means on a real lawn.

products.name: Craftsman V20 13 in. String Trimmer and Edger Kit, 4Ah Battery and Charger
products.description:
The Craftsman is the best-balanced kit because every part of the box is generous. A 4Ah V20 battery is large for a trimmer of this class, a 13 inch swath is the standard size for a mid-sized lawn and the head converts to an edger. The maker quotes up to 63 minutes of runtime, the longest claim in this guide.

Treat the number as a ceiling. Runtime figures assume a fresh pack and light grass, and thick or wet growth will cut the time substantially, but even half of 63 minutes is enough for most suburban lawns. The 52 percent more power claim is relative to an earlier model, so it tells you the tool improved rather than what the absolute output is.

V20 is a widely stocked platform, so a spare pack or a bare tool for the hedge is easy to find and fits the same charger. Clean the head after each session, check the line length before you start and store the battery indoors over winter. For a buyer who wants one safe choice, this is it. Because the kit includes a full-size battery rather than a token one, the charger sits idle less often, and the tool is ready on the weekend without planning. Expect the pack to last several seasons if you avoid leaving it fully charged in a hot shed.
products.bestFor: Mid-sized lawns where one well-sized battery should finish the job.
pros: 4Ah battery is large for a trimmer kit
Up to 63 minutes of runtime claimed
cons: Runtime claim is a best case
Power claim is relative to an older model

products.name: Cordless 3-in-1 Weed Wacker Kit, 880W Motor, 18,000 RPM, Two 4.0Ah Batteries and Fast Charger
products.description:
Two 4.0Ah batteries and a fast charger make this the biggest kit by energy in the guide. The maker lists an 880W motor and 18,000 RPM, both no-load figures that describe the motor's spec rather than the cutting force, and a three-in-one design that works as a trimmer, weed cutter and mini mower.

The two packs are the practical benefit. You can rotate them, so one charges while the other works, and the fast charger shortens the wait. That is what turns a long yard into a one-session job. Combined, 8Ah of capacity is the most you get at this level.

The seller is a smaller brand, so parts and warranty support are the unknowns. Read the return terms, keep the receipt and test the tool on a small patch first. Clear grass from the head after use and store both packs indoors. Because the motor labels are no-load numbers, judge the tool on how it handles your own grass in the first week. Keep the original packaging for the return window in case the cutting performance does not match your expectations.
products.bestFor: Larger lawns where runtime matters more than brand.
pros: Three modes including a mini mower

products.name: Greenworks 24V 12 in. 2-in-1 Trimmer and Edger Kit, 2.0Ah, Telescoping Shaft
products.description:
The Greenworks kit is the one to give a beginner. The head switches from trimming to edging with one button and no tools, pivots 90 degrees for edging around roots and beds, and the aluminium shaft telescopes to suit shorter and taller users.

The 2.0Ah battery is the smallest of the premium-brand kits here, so it suits a small to medium lawn and not a half-acre. That makes the telescoping shaft and quick conversion the real attractions: it is a tool you can set up for yourself in a minute and use without a manual.

A spare battery is a sensible add-on for larger yards. The 24V platform is smaller than the 40V line, so there are fewer matching tools. Clean the pivot after use and store the pack indoors. The telescoping shaft also makes it the easiest kit to put away, since it shortens to fit a cupboard. Owners often add a second 24V battery within a season, so budget for one if your lawn is more than a few hundred square feet.

products.name: 20,000 RPM Cordless 4-in-1 Weed Wacker, 800W Claim, LED Display, Wheels, 2 x 3000mAh
products.description:
The LED display is the useful detail. It shows the battery state, so you know when to swap packs before the tool dies mid-job. Two 21V 3000mAh batteries give 6000mAh combined, and the maker claims up to 90 to 120 minutes of runtime, a wide range that should be treated with caution.

A headline of 20,000 RPM and 800W is a motor label and not a measure of cutting force, and the listing notes that the cutting width depends on the set-up, at a maximum of 11 to 12 inches with the edging wheel. That honesty is helpful, since it tells you the swath is not as wide as some competitors advertise.

It is a four-in-one with wheels, so it offers more modes than a simple trimmer, but also more parts to keep clean. Check the wheel and the attachments after each use, charge both packs before a session and store them indoors. The display is most valuable when you work in short, planned stints, because you can swap at the first low-battery warning instead of waiting for the tool to stall. That habit is gentler on lithium cells than running them to zero.
products.bestFor: Users who like to see charge levels and have a mixed yard.
cons: Narrow actual swath of 11 to 12 in.

products.name: 21V 12 in. Cordless String Trimmer, 2.5Ah Battery and Fast Charger, 9,500 RPM, Auto Feed
products.description:
A 2.5Ah battery with a fast charger is the key pairing here. The pack is a little larger than the 2.0Ah kits, and the charger shortens the gap between sessions, which suits a small yard that you trim in two halves. The motor is rated at 9,500 RPM and the 12 inch head has automatic line feed.

Automatic feed is the feature that makes a basic trimmer pleasant: the line is released as it shortens, so there is no bumping. The 21V label is a platform name like 20V MAX and not a step up in power.

It is a light, simple kit from a smaller brand, and one battery is all you get. Check the warranty, wipe the head after use and store the pack indoors. If your lawn needs more than one pack, order a second battery at the same time, since the fast charger only helps if there is a spare to swap in. Used that way, it behaves like a much dearer kit.
products.bestFor: Small yards where a fast charger fills the gaps.

products.name: 20V 12 in. 3-in-1 Cordless Weed Wacker, 3.5 lb, Two 2.0Ah Batteries and Quick Charger
products.description:
This kit is the lightest at 3.5 pounds, and it ships with two 2.0Ah batteries and a quick charger. The pair gives 4Ah in total, which is the same energy as one 4Ah pack but with the advantage that you can swap and rest. A 12 inch head converts between trimmer, edger and weed cutter.

The light weight and two packs suit anyone who works in short bursts. It is not a high-power machine, so the match is a small to medium lawn and ordinary weeds. As with other budget kits, check the warranty and the availability of spare batteries.

Clean the head after each use, charge both packs before a session and store them indoors. Treat it as a tool for regular maintenance, not for cutting back an overgrown plot. Its two small packs are best rotated every session so they age together. If one pack drops off early, replace both rather than running a mismatched pair.
products.bestFor: Small lawns and users who want a light tool and two packs.
pros: Two 2.0Ah batteries and a quick charger
Trimmer, edger and weed cutter modes

buyingCriteria.explanation: The battery sets how long you can cut. Capacity is the one spec that directly sets how long the tool works, so rank kits by it before you look at anything else. A kit with a big pack and plain motor beats one with a flashy motor and a small pack. The Craftsman includes a 4Ah pack, the 3-in-1 kit two 4.0Ah packs, the 4-in-1 two 3000mAh packs and the Greenworks a 2.0Ah pack. For a half-acre, aim for 4Ah or two packs.

Two packs let you rest while one charges. Three of the six kits ship with two. A single pack means you wait or buy a spare, so count the cost of a second battery into any single-pack kit. Two packs also spread wear: each is used half as often, so the pair can outlast a single pack that is cycled every session.

A fast charger shortens the gap between sessions. The 3-in-1 kit and the 21V kit include fast chargers and the 20V 3.5 lb kit a quick charger. A slow charger on a big pack can leave you waiting for hours. If the listing does not state a charge time, assume a standard charger and plan for several hours. A fast charger matters most when you own a single spare.

The Craftsman claims up to 63 minutes and the 4-in-1 up to 90 to 120 minutes on two packs. These are best-case figures. Dense growth, wet grass and cold weather can halve them. A claim given as a range, as with 90 to 120 minutes, tells you the maker is describing a best case. Use these numbers only to compare kits, not to plan your Saturday.

Motor labels such as 880W, 800W, 18,000 RPM and 20,000 RPM describe a no-load spec and not the cutting force. Torque under load decides how a trimmer behaves, so compare swath and battery rather than the biggest number.

V20 and Greenworks 24V packs are widely stocked, while kits from small brands often have a single supplier. Check that spare batteries can be bought before you commit. A kit whose only battery is discontinued becomes a paperweight after a few years. Choose a platform with a track record if you plan to keep the tool for a decade.

howWeEvaluated.title: Box contents
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared battery size, count and charger type for each kit. The Craftsman and the two 4.0Ah kit scored highest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We read each runtime claim against the pack size. Claims were treated as best cases and compared with each other. We did not add them up or convert them to minutes per acre, since the conditions behind each figure are not given.

howWeEvaluated.title: Convenience
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at feed, conversion and shaft adjustment. The Greenworks telescoping shaft scored well.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how widely each battery is used. V20 scored well and small-brand kits lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Honesty of listing
howWeEvaluated.description: We rewarded listings that state real figures such as the 4-in-1's cutting width. Vague claims scored lower. A listing that admits a limit, for example that the swath changes with the edging wheel fitted, earns more trust than one that quotes only the largest number.

howToChoose.subheading: One Big Pack vs Two Packs

cards.label: One big pack
cards.text: The Craftsman 4Ah has a single large battery. It is simple, but you wait for a recharge once it empties.

cards.label: Two packs
cards.text: The 3-in-1 and 4-in-1 kits have two packs. You can swap and keep working.

howToChoose.note: Choose one big pack for mid-sized lawns and two packs for larger ones.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for two packs or a 4Ah battery, plus a fast charger. Count the packs per mow.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The two 4.0Ah kit provides 8Ah and a fast charger, and the Craftsman gives a 4Ah pack with a claimed 63 minutes.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if you want an established platform and spares, as with the Craftsman V20.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you want runtime on a budget. The two-pack kits give more energy for less.

maintenance.why: Store packs at half charge. A full or empty pack ages faster, and a pack left flat for months may refuse to charge. Keep them in a dry room away from frost.
Packed grass strains the motor and holds moisture against the housing. Clear it with the battery removed and let the head dry before storage.
Short line cuts a smaller swath and loads the motor unevenly. Keep a spare spool of the correct diameter where you store the tool.
A frayed lead is a hazard. Replace it.
Grit stiffens moving parts on 3-in-1 and 4-in-1 models.

faq.a: At minimum a battery and charger. Better kits add a second battery and a fast charger.

faq.q: How big a battery do I need?
faq.a: For a half-acre, aim for 4Ah or two packs. A single 2.0Ah pack suits a small lawn.
They are useful for comparison. Real runtime is shorter in thick or wet growth.
They are no-load labels. Use swath and battery size to judge a tool, not the biggest number.

faq.q: Can I buy a spare battery?
faq.a: For V20 and Greenworks, yes, easily. For small brands, check before buying.

faq.q: Is a fast charger worth it?
faq.a: Yes if you want to finish a larger lawn in one day. It refills a pack while you use the other.
